name: h5scope
description: A Qt-based viewer for HDF5 files.
$comment-qtbase: qtbase is named twice because a feature list cannot be qualified by
platform, only a dependency can. The X11, Wayland, EGL and fontconfig
features below do not exist for a Windows triplet, and asking for them
there does not degrade -- it fails to resolve the manifest at all.
The Windows list is the Linux one minus exactly those, and minus dbus,
which is there for the Linux desktop's file dialog alone: see
$comment-dbus below. Windows draws its own native dialog out of the
platform plugin already on the link line. freetype is kept
although Qt on Windows draws its glyphs through DirectWrite by default,
because dropping it would also drop brotli and bzip2, which reach the
link line only as freetype's dependencies. Keeping it makes the Windows
dependency set a strict subset of the Linux one, and that is what lets
bundle describe two platforms without describing them separately.
$comment-dbus: qtbase's dbus feature is what builds the xdg-desktop-portal platform
theme, which is the only native file dialog a static Qt can carry on
Linux: GTK's would make libgtk-3 a dependency of the binary, and a
dynamic Qt finds the desktop's own through plugins this one cannot load.
The feature on its own would link libdbus-1. vcpkg's dbus port builds
only a shared library, so that would put libdbus-1.so.3 in the binary's
NEEDED list -- a library the loader then refuses to start without, which
is the failure ports/xcb-util-cursor exists to avoid. The triplets in
cmake/triplets therefore build qtbase with -DINPUT_dbus=runtime, so Qt
opens libdbus with dlopen when there is one and goes without D-Bus when
there is not. tools/ci/verify-binary.sh asserts the NEEDED entry stays
So the dbus port is built but never linked, and is listed below without
its default features only to keep its systemd feature -- and with it
libsystemd -- out of a build that would not use it either.
